Incident Bot: ALERT: queue growth on gpu-infer-prod -> routing to #incidents and paging @oncall. metric: inference_queue_length up 12x in 5m, token throughput down 60% :rotating_light:

Alex R: I'm on it, looking at autoscaler logs and scheduler rejects. I see a bunch of Pending pods with reason: "Insufficient MIG" and "Binpack constraints".

Priya S: Confirming. Autoscaler tried to scale but hit per-region GPU quota and some node groups returned capacity available but pods couldn't schedule.

Jamie L: Logs show many nodes with mixed MIG profiles (1g.5g and 2g configured). Our binpacker placement requires exact MIG match, so leftover slices are incompatible -> stranded fractional GPU capacity.

Sylvia M: Which pool?

Alex R: dedicated-batch-01 and shared-hosted-02. Example pod failed: 
```
Name: inference-worker-7f8d
Reason: 0/48 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient MIG, 28 MatchPredicate fails.
```

Priya S: Autoscaler error: "cannot provision MIG slice: instance quota reached". Also note we hit a soft throttle: scale-api returning 429 on repeated create attempts.

Elena C (CS): Customer impact — three enterprise customers in EU region reporting 5xxs and high tail latency. CS ticket #CS-4921 opened and alerted.

Jamie L: Quick triage plan: 1) Pause low-priority batch queues 2) Temporarily raise autoscaler max-replicas for the affected pool 3) Evict preemptible jobs to consolidate contiguous MIGs 4) If needed, trigger a rolling MIG resize on a subset to unify slice sizes.

Alex R: Implementing step 1 and 2 now. Patching autoscaler bounds: `kubectl patch hpa autoscaler-dedicated-batch -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":200}}'` (helm diff applied).

Priya S: I'm throttling create calls at the control-plane level to avoid thrash. Reducing autoscaler frequency to 30s.

Incident Bot: ACTION REQUIRED: oncall handoff in 15m. Current severity: P1 - service degradation, active mitigation.

Sylvia M: We should avoid immediate MIG resize unless we can migrate with minimal downtime. Alternative: emergency binpack relaxation to allow scheduling into slightly larger MIG slices (fallthrough policy). I'll push a conservative scheduler-config change to allow 1g pods onto 2g MIGs with overcommit flag for 10m.

Jamie L: Doing the scheduler change now: editing ConfigMap `binpacker-config` -> set `allow_mismatch_temporarily: true` and `mismatch_ttl_s: 600`. Applying.

Alex R: Seeing a drop in Pending pods after the config change. Queue length still high but decreasing. Latency for impacted customers trending down from 1200ms to ~420ms.

Elena C: Noting customer comms: emailed impacted customers with a brief summary and ETA for full recovery (EOD). CS will update ticket.

Priya S: Observed side-effect: a few high-memory tasks scheduled into mismatched slices triggered OOM kills. Rolling back mismatch policy for teams requiring strict memory. Applying label-based exemption for memory-sensitive pods.

Jamie L: Next step: plan controlled maintenance window to standardize MIG profiles across that cluster pool. Proposal: cordon subset of nodes, remigrate critical jobs to host-pools, destroy and recreate nodes with uniform MIG size (1g) then uncordon. Estimated time 45-60m for each node subset.

Alex R: I'll coordinate the maintenance. For now set routing fallback to smaller models for non-enterprise traffic to conserve GPU tokens. Patching routing policy to route non-SLA traffic to cheap-embed endpoints.

Incident Bot: NOTE: handoff to next oncall (Priya S) at 3190012800. Timeline: mitigation in-progress, root cause likely MIG-slice layout + autoscaler throttle.

Priya S: Acknowledged handoff. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate the node re-provisioning with infra.

Sylvia M: Creating a follow-up ticket for longer-term fixes: 1) autoscaler backoff improvements, 2) binpacker to be MIG-aware with defragmentation heuristics, 3) capacity planner to avoid mixed MIG sizes in the same pool.

Elena C: CS asks for postmortem and customer impact summary once resolved.

Alex R: Current status: queue length down to 2.3x baseline, affected customers recovering. Keeping cluster in emergency config for 30m, then gradual rollback. Will post updates here. :white_check_mark:
